The test image spots are larger than tar spot dots and look most similar to Physoderma brown spot. Let me check a few more candidates:

Now I have enough evidence to make my assessment.

**Analysis Summary:**

Test image features:
- Close-up of a corn leaf sheath/midrib area
- Dark brown to black, oval/circular spots (5-8mm) scattered on green tissue
- Spots are embedded in tissue, not raised/powdery
- Some brown discoloration of surrounding tissue

Ruling out:
- **Tar_spot**: Reference shows tiny pin-point black dots, far smaller and more numerous than test image
- **Common_rust / Southern_rust**: Orange/red powdery pustules — completely different color
- **Northern_corn_leaf_blight**: Cigar-shaped elongated lesions
- **Anthracnose_leaf_spot**: Larger spindle-shaped lesions with tan centers
- **Eyespot**: Small spots with yellow halos, tan centers
- **Holcus_spot**: White/tan spots with lighter centers

**Best match — Physoderma_brown_spot**: The Physoderma reference (bottom-right panel) shows exactly this pattern: dark brown to black oval spots on the leaf sheath/midrib area of corn. The symptom description states "dark purplish to black oval spots also occur on the midrib" — matching the test image closely. The size, color (dark brown-black), shape (oval), and location (sheath/midrib) all align.
